faqs.question: Do we need a photographer for a pumpkin head photoshoot?
faqs.answer: No. Neither wearer can see the camera well, so a phone on a tripod with a 10-second timer, or one friend acting as helper and spotter, is enough for all seven frames.

faqs.question: How heavy is a real pumpkin head?
faqs.answer: Utah State University Extension lists common carving varieties at 18 to 25 lb, about 8 to 11 kg, before scooping. That is several times the 2.85 kg helmet load that produced neck fatigue in a 45-minute lab study, so wear foam and keep real pumpkins as props.

faqs.question: Can you see out of a pumpkin head?
faqs.answer: Only if you cut the eyes at your real eye line. Have your partner mark your pupils with a washable pen while the pumpkin is on, cut larger than looks right, and back the holes with black mesh so the camera sees a dark eye but you see your footing.

faqs.question: How do you breathe in a pumpkin head?
faqs.answer: Add 4 to 6 holes about 1 cm wide at mouth height and under the chin line, hidden inside the carved grin. Take the head off between frames and never put a candle inside one you are wearing.

faqs.question: What size hole do you cut for your head?
faqs.answer: Measure your head circumference above the ears, divide by 3.14, and add about 2 cm so it slides over hair. A ring of soft foam inside the crown stops it resting on your nose.

faqs.question: What time should we shoot a pumpkin head photoshoot on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Start in the last hour before sunset and finish in blue hour. On 31 October sunset is about 17:55 in New York, 16:37 in London, 19:23 in Sydney and 18:06 in Mumbai, with 22 to 33 minutes of twilight after it.

faqs.question: How do you pose when nobody can see your faces?
faqs.answer: Use whole-head angles and hands. Gaze research going back to Wollaston in 1824 shows the angle of the head outline pulls where viewers think a face is looking, so turning the pumpkin 30 degrees toward your partner reads as a look.

faqs.question: Can kids do a pumpkin head photoshoot?
faqs.answer: Not with a worn real pumpkin; a child's neck should carry nothing like an 18 lb load. Let children hold a 0.5 to 1.5 lb mini pumpkin or wear a light papier-mâché shell for a few seconds with an adult beside them.

faqs.question: How should we post our pumpkin head couple photos?
faqs.answer: Crop them tall, at 4:5 or 9:16, since 48.3% of SubhSandesh page views come from phones. If the photos are for one person, a private page with a password keeps them out of public feeds; 38.5% of creators add one.

faqs.question: How long does a pumpkin head couple photoshoot take?
faqs.answer: Plan about 1 hour to make two foam heads and about 45 minutes to shoot, timed to finish as blue hour ends. Real pumpkins add about 2 hours of carving and cleanup.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Pumpkin Head Couple Photoshoot: How to Make, Wear and Light It

A pumpkin head couple photoshoot works best with two hollow foam craft pumpkins, not real ones, shot in the 22 to 33 minutes of blue hour after sunset on or near 31 October. Crop every frame tall, because 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, and plan for privacy: 38.5% of creators add a password before sending a page. A real carving pumpkin weighs 18 to 25 lb, several times the helmet load that tired volunteers' necks in a 45-minute lab study.

Below: the trend's origin, building a head you can see through, a seven-frame shot list, twilight times for four cities, and editing.

## Where did the pumpkin head photoshoot trend come from?

A pumpkin head photoshoot is a portrait session in which the subjects wear hollowed pumpkins over their whole heads, with carved faces standing in for their own. The couple version pairs two carved faces, so the pumpkins carry all the expression.

The earliest dated news report we found is [FOX 13 Tampa Bay's story of 30 October 2020](https://www.fox13news.com/news/festive-photoshoot-brings-needed-laughs-and-smiles-during-pandemic). It describes photographer Jennifer Sapountsis shooting friends whose carved pumpkins had "a hole in the bottom big enough to fit over their heads", framed as a way to make people laugh during the pandemic. We could not verify any earlier origin, so treat claims that the trend began elsewhere as unconfirmed (checked 14 October 2026).

## Real pumpkin or foam craft pumpkin: which head should you wear?

[Utah State University Extension's 2020 pumpkin fact sheet](https://extension.usu.edu/yardandgarden/research/pumpkins-in-the-garden) puts common carving varieties such as Connecticut Field at 18 to 25 lb, about 8 to 11 kg. Smaller types like Jack Be Little weigh 0.5 to 1.5 lb, which makes them props for hands, not heads.

For scale, a 2024 [Experimental Physiology study of helmet load on the neck](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11442774) had 20 volunteers wear a 2.85 kg helmet assembly for 45 minutes. Women showed greater neck-muscle fatigue and men a measurable drop in cervical disc height afterwards. Even if scooping removes a fair share of the flesh, a head-sized real pumpkin sits well above that load, and it is balanced on the head rather than strapped to it.

The table compares four head options on weight, wear time and prep. Weights marked USU come from the fact sheet; the rest are our estimates.

| Head option | Weight on the neck | Wear time we suggest | Prep time for two |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real carving pumpkin, scooped | Starts at 18–25 lb (8–11 kg) before scooping, per USU | 1–2 minute bursts, seated | About 2 hours, plus cleanup |
| Foam craft pumpkin, hollow | Our estimate: under 1 kg; check the label | 10–15 minutes between breaks | About 1 hour |
| Papier-mâché shell on a balloon | Our estimate: 300–600 g | 15 minutes between breaks | 2 evenings, for drying |
| Small real pumpkin held, not worn | 0.5–1.5 lb (0.2–0.7 kg), per USU | No limit | 10 minutes |

The takeaway: wear foam or papier-mâché, and let real pumpkins appear in hands, on steps or at your feet. Wear-time figures are our working rules, not clinical limits.

## How do you cut a pumpkin head you can see and breathe through?

The same five cuts apply to foam and real pumpkins. Measure first, because a head that tilts or slips ruins more frames than bad light.

- **Neck hole:** measure head circumference above the ears, divide by 3.14 for the width, and add 2 cm so it slides over hair.
- **Eye line:** with the pumpkin on, have your partner mark where your pupils sit with a washable pen. Cut from that mark, not from where the pumpkin's middle looks to be.
- **Sight holes:** cut the carved eyes larger than looks right, then back them with black mesh fabric. It hides your face but shows your footing.
- **Breathing holes:** add 4 to 6 holes, about 1 cm wide, at mouth height and under the chin line, hidden in the carved grin.
- **Padding:** glue a ring of soft foam or a folded sock inside the crown so the head rests on your skull, not your nose.

Never put a candle or any flame inside a worn head. If you want a glow, it comes from outside, covered in the shot list below.

Neither wearer can see the camera well, so use a helper or a tripod with a 10-second timer. Short sessions are safer sessions.

## A seven-frame shot list for two pumpkin heads

A carved face cannot change expression, so direction has to come from the head angle and the hands. Research on gaze backs this up: [Otsuka and colleagues' 2014 study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4120707) reviews evidence, back to Wollaston's 1824 drawings, that the angle of the head outline pulls where viewers think a face is looking. Turn the whole pumpkin toward your partner, and the carved eyes read as a look. Each frame below lists the setup, the head angle and the hold time.

### 1. The slow turn

- **Setup:** both seated on a low wall, facing the camera, hands in laps.
- **Head angle:** take one frame straight on, then one where the right-hand person turns 30 degrees toward the other.
- **Hold:** 5 seconds per frame, then heads off.

### 2. One head off

- **Setup:** one wears the pumpkin; the other holds theirs in their lap, own face visible and laughing.
- **Head angle:** the masked partner looks down at the empty pumpkin.
- **Hold:** 30 seconds; switch roles for a pair of frames.

### 3. Errand run

- **Setup:** both walking a quiet pavement carrying paper grocery bags.
- **Head angle:** both forward, mid-stride; the joke is how ordinary it is.
- **Hold:** 3 short passes of 20 metres each.

### 4. Reading over a shoulder

- **Setup:** one sits on porch steps with a book; the other stands behind.
- **Head angle:** both tilted down 20 degrees toward the page.
- **Hold:** 10 seconds.

### 5. The face swap

- **Setup:** carve two different faces, then trade heads for half the set.
- **Head angle:** both straight at the camera, arms crossed, as if nothing changed.
- **Hold:** 5 seconds; caption it as a before-and-after pair.

### 6. Lantern between you

- **Setup:** a small real jack-o'-lantern with a tea light sits on the ground between your feet; this is the only flame in the shoot.
- **Head angle:** both turned down toward it, so the glow catches the pumpkin skins from below.
- **Hold:** 3 seconds, at blue hour, with the phone braced.

### 7. Walking away

- **Setup:** hand in hand down a path or driveway, backs to the camera.
- **Head angle:** one looks back over a shoulder; a whole-head turn of 90 degrees reads clearly from behind.
- **Hold:** 2 or 3 passes.

## When is golden hour and blue hour on 31 October?

Golden hour is a photographer's convention for roughly the last hour before sunset, not an astronomical term. Blue hour here means sunset to the end of civil twilight, when the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon. These times come from [the Sunrise-Sunset.org calculation API](https://sunrise-sunset.org/api), retrieved 14 October 2026, in local clock time.

- **New York:** sunset 17:55 EDT both years; civil twilight ends 18:22. US clocks change on 1 November 2026 and 7 November 2027, so Halloween stays on daylight time.
- **London:** sunset 16:37 GMT in 2026 and 16:38 in 2027; twilight ends 17:10 and 17:11. Clocks go back on 25 October 2026 and in the early hours of Halloween itself in 2027.
- **Sydney:** sunset 19:23 AEDT in 2026 and 19:22 in 2027; twilight ends 19:48 and 19:47.
- **Mumbai:** sunset 18:06 IST in 2026 and 18:07 in 2027; twilight ends 18:28 both years.

That gives you 22 to 33 minutes of blue hour, enough for about four frames with breaks. Shoot frames 1, 3 and 5 in the golden hour, then 6 and 7 once the sky turns blue. With no faces showing, you need only enough light to keep orange skins orange.

## How should you edit and post the set?

Edit all frames with one preset so the pumpkins match from frame to frame. Warm the white balance slightly, lift the shadows inside the carved eyes so they read as holes rather than black blotches, and keep grain natural.

Crop each frame to a tall 4:5 or 9:16, because 48.3% of SubhSandesh views come from phones and a wide frame shrinks two pumpkins to dots. Post the face swap as a pair.

If the set is for one person rather than your followers, a [Halloween card with up to six photos](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about five minutes and walks them through a little haunted house, ending in "Will you be my boo?". For a full set, the [premium Halloween page with up to 12 photos and a 60-second voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about ten minutes and can stay locked behind a countdown until 31 October.

Both are one-person greeting pages, not party tools or a public gallery. If your photos are not Halloween-specific, the ["I love you" page](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) is the most-viewed SubhSandesh template, with 29.7% of all page views.

Timing helps here too. Our only festival lead-time data is from Raksha Bandhan 2026, a different festival with just 89 pages: 49.4% were built on the day itself. Shoot the weekend before so the set is edited before the rush.

## When is a pumpkin head shoot the wrong plan?

Skip worn heads entirely if either of you has neck pain, a recent neck injury or a dislike of enclosed spaces. Frame 2 and frame 6 work with the pumpkins held, and the set still reads as a pumpkin head shoot.

It is also a poor plan for young children, whose necks should carry nothing like an 18 lb load, and for hot evenings like a Mumbai October, when a sealed head gets stuffy within minutes. And a SubhSandesh page loses to a print whenever you live together: a framed 8x10 of frame 5 on the hallway wall will be seen far more than 11.1 times, the average views per page on the platform.

## Sources

- FOX 13 Tampa Bay, *Festive photoshoot brings needed laughs and smiles during pandemic*, 30 October 2020
- Hefelbower and Drost, Utah State University Extension, *Pumpkins in the Garden*, February 2020
- Yin et al., *Experimental Physiology*, 2024, helmet load and the neck
- Otsuka et al., *Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance*, 2014, head orientation and perceived gaze
- Sunrise-Sunset.org API, sunset and civil twilight times, retrieved 14 October 2026
